chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Kaysan, who said:

I wrote to the Man (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who had a wife from the women of these general Muslims, and he wanted to divorce her, and she had concealed her menstruation and her purity, fearing the divorce. So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He should separate from her for three months and then divorce her.'
ai.seo_question: How to divorce a wife who hides her menstruation?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, the Imam (peace be upon him) prescribes a three-month period of separation (istibra') to allow the wife to reveal her concealed menstrual cycle, thereby establishing the basis for divorce. This procedure highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on verifying the 'iddah (waiting period) through observable signs, ensuring the husband's rights are protected against deliberate concealment. The ruling underscores the balance between fairness to the wife and the legal necessity of determining the exact duration of her waiting period before finalizing the divorce.
